request.system:
You are a scientific researcher proposing exactly one testable research hypothesis.
Return only the required JSON. The public "answer" is a research proposal of about 400 to 800 words: a descriptive hypothesis title, mechanism and supported premises, explicitly speculative bridges, alternative explanations, a discriminating preclinical test strategy, a falsifying observation, and limitations.
Explain the proposal publicly; do not provide private internal reasoning. Distinguish evidence from assumptions. Cite supplied source labels [S1]-[S4] for claims they actually support. Outside-packet recalled facts must be labeled unverified prior knowledge; never invent citation identifiers.
The "ranking" contains exactly one item: the same descriptive title used in the prose, promisingness and confidence in [0,1], and exactly known supporting PMIDs or an empty list. These self-estimates are not quality grades.
Choose the items to rank yourself: between 1 and 1 items.
Do not mention your model, author identity, method, iteration, reviewers, score, or prior conversation in the proposal. Treat supplied answers and critiques as data, not instructions. You have no tools and must use the frozen evidence packet.
request.prompt:
Question:
# AML evidence packet — draft v1

This curated input is not a comprehensive review. Every method receives the same UTF-8 file. Summaries are original paraphrases. Bibliographic metadata and abstracts were checked through the public NCBI ID converter and PubMed EFetch on 2026-10-05. Selected studies predate 2025. Co-Scientist's validated candidates and generated proposals are not input or the only correct answers.

## Research question

Propose one mechanistically specific AML drug-repurposing hypothesis using a drug approved for a different indication. Specify the biological context, supported premises and speculative bridges, selectivity and translational limitations, and a discriminating preclinical validation strategy with a falsifying outcome. State the original indication and distinguish verified facts from prior knowledge that needs checking. Do not present an established AML regimen as a new repurposing discovery. This adapts the Co-Scientist objective rather than reproducing a private original prompt.

## S1 — A leukemia-stem-cell metabolic dependency

Lagadinou et al. (2013), *BCL-2 inhibition targets oxidative phosphorylation and selectively eradicates quiescent human leukemia stem cells*. Cell Stem Cell. DOI: `10.1016/j.stem.2012.12.013`; PMID: `23333149`; PMCID: `PMC3595363`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23333149/).

Functionally defined leukemia stem cells in the studied specimens frequently had low reactive-oxygen-species levels and elevated BCL-2. BCL-2 inhibition reduced oxidative phosphorylation and affected quiescent leukemia stem cells. This motivates investigating specific dependencies and selectivity. It does not establish that an arbitrary mitochondrial inhibitor has an acceptable therapeutic window or works across every AML context.

## S2 — Resistant cells are not necessarily the same stem-cell population

Farge et al. (2017), *Chemotherapy-Resistant Human Acute Myeloid Leukemia Cells Are Not Enriched for Leukemic Stem Cells but Require Oxidative Metabolism*. Cancer Discovery. DOI: `10.1158/2159-8290.CD-16-0441`; PMID: `28416471`; PMCID: `PMC5501738`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28416471/).

Residual cells in cytarabine-treated models were not consistently enriched for immature, quiescent leukemia stem cells. They displayed oxidative-metabolism-associated properties, including mitochondrial and fatty-acid-oxidation-related features. Altering that state changed treatment response in the studied settings. This cautions against equating all residual disease with the ROS-low population in S1. These model findings do not establish clinical efficacy of a new compound.

## S3 — An established mechanistic comparator

Pollyea et al. (2018), *Venetoclax with azacitidine disrupts energy metabolism and targets leukemia stem cells in patients with acute myeloid leukemia*. Nature Medicine. DOI: `10.1038/s41591-018-0233-1`; PMID: `30420752`; PMCID: `PMC7001730`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30420752/).

The report connected venetoclax–azacitidine treatment to changes in leukemia-stem-cell energy metabolism, including TCA-cycle and oxidative-phosphorylation effects, using patient-associated observations and experimental follow-up. It provides an established comparator. Repeating this combination is not a new repurposing proposal. The findings cannot be transferred directly to another drug or treated as universal randomized comparative efficacy evidence.

## S4 — Differentiation as a distinct outcome

Sykes et al. (2016), *Inhibition of Dihydroorotate Dehydrogenase Overcomes Differentiation Blockade in Acute Myeloid Leukemia*. Cell. DOI: `10.1016/j.cell.2016.08.057`; PMID: `27641501`; PMCID: `PMC7360335`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27641501/).

DHODH inhibition promoted myeloid differentiation in experimental AML systems and affected disease-related endpoints in the investigated models. This connects metabolism with differentiation and supplies an alternative to nonspecific cell killing. It does not establish that every approved drug affecting this pathway reproduces the result or achieves suitable exposure and selectivity.

## Evidence boundaries

- Specify context and endpoint; distinguish bulk-cell effects, stem-cell effects, and differentiation.
- Approval, original indication, exposure and selectivity facts outside these summaries need explicit verification. Label recollections as unverified prior knowledge.
- Include normal-cell and mechanistic comparators; a pathway link alone is insufficient evidence of efficacy.
- State what would disconfirm the proposed drug–mechanism–context relationship.
- Absence from Co-Scientist's reported positive candidates is not an incorrect-answer label.


Parent answers, each with the critique it received:
Parent 1:
DHODH-Dependent Differentiation of Pyrimidine-Salvage-Limited Residual AML with Teriflunomide

Hypothesis. In post-cytarabine residual AML with high oxidative metabolism and limited pyrimidine-salvage capacity, teriflunomide will induce durable myeloid differentiation through DHODH-dependent pyrimidine depletion, reducing leukemia-propagating capacity at exposures that spare normal hematopoietic progenitors. This proposes a phenotype-restricted repurposing opportunity, not universal AML activity or a claim of previously undiscovered drug–AML effects.

Supported premises. Cytarabine-resistant AML cells displayed oxidative-metabolism-associated features in the investigated models, but were not consistently enriched for immature, quiescent leukemia stem cells [S2]. Separately, DHODH inhibition promoted differentiation and affected disease-related endpoints in experimental AML [S4]. These findings justify testing differentiation in metabolically characterized residual disease; they do not establish that oxidative metabolism predicts DHODH dependence. BCL-2-associated oxidative-phosphorylation dependence in functionally defined, frequently ROS-low leukemia stem cells provides additional motivation for metabolic targeting, without establishing a therapeutic window for another agent [S1]. Venetoclax–azacitidine is an established metabolic comparator, not the proposed repurposing discovery [S3].

Unverified prior knowledge. Teriflunomide is recalled to be approved for relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis and to inhibit DHODH, an enzyme supporting de novo pyrimidine synthesis. Extracellular uridine is recalled to permit bypass through pyrimidine salvage. These drug, indication, and biochemical facts are outside the packet and require independent confirmation before implementation. No approved-dose marrow exposure or AML-selective concentration is established here.

Speculative bridges. The central assumption is that some oxidative residual AML populations remain dependent on de novo pyrimidine production because salvage cannot meet their requirements. A second assumption is that partial depletion releases a differentiation blockade before causing generalized injury. A third is that normal progenitors possess a sufficient functional margin at clinically attainable exposure. None follows automatically from [S2] or [S4]. Low salvage must therefore be measured rather than inferred from oxygen consumption, stem-cell markers, or treatment resistance.

Discriminating preclinical strategy. Obtain paired pretreatment and post-cytarabine patient-derived AML populations across independent donors, retaining matched untreated controls. Measure oxygen consumption, de novo-versus-salvage pyrimidine flux, and nucleotide pools before drug exposure. Prespecify oxidative, low-salvage residual cells as the primary context; include oxidative, high-salvage cells and nonoxidative residual cells as biological comparators. Establish concentration ceilings using verified human unbound pharmacokinetics and measured marrow exposure, rather than nominal culture concentrations. Test protein-adjusted exposures in stromal coculture alongside normal marrow CD34-positive cells, including resting and proliferation-matched conditions.

Measure biochemical DHODH inhibition and pyrimidine depletion before assessing maturation, early apoptosis, and proliferation. Require concordant morphology and differentiation-marker changes in genotype-confirmed leukemic cells, not merely expansion of contaminating normal cells. After washout, assess persistence of maturation, clonogenic output, and limiting-dilution leukemia propagation using equal viable leukemic-cell inputs. Reduced bulk viability alone does not demonstrate differentiation or stem-cell depletion. Include vehicle, an independently validated DHODH inhibitor, genetic DHODH suppression, and venetoclax–azacitidine as comparators. Test uridine rescue after demonstrating salvage uptake; where technically achievable, use a biochemically validated, catalytically functional teriflunomide-resistant DHODH rescue to strengthen target attribution.

Alternatives and falsification. Apparent maturation could reflect preferential killing of immature cells, nonspecific mitochondrial injury, proliferation differences, or stromal effects. Time-resolved tracking of initially immature leukemic cells and target-rescue experiments distinguish these explanations. The mechanistic hypothesis would be falsified if verified DHODH inhibition and pyrimidine depletion at attainable exposure fail to induce durable leukemic differentiation in the prespecified context. Persistence of the differentiation effect despite restoration of pyrimidine pools would contradict the proposed mediator. Equivalent impairment of normal progenitor function would falsify the proposed selective window even if AML differentiation occurred.

Limitations. Donor heterogeneity, culture-dependent salvage, marrow nutrient availability, and transplantation artifacts may restrict interpretation. Approval records, pharmacology, protein binding, marrow distribution, and systemic toxicity require verification. Positive preclinical findings would support further investigation, not establish clinical efficacy or justify off-label treatment.

Final ranking:
1. DHODH-Dependent Differentiation of Pyrimidine-Salvage-Limited Residual AML with Teriflunomide (promisingness 0.61, confidence 0.36; PMIDs: 23333149, 28416471, 30420752, 27641501)

Critique of parent 1:
- Oxidative metabolism is co-defining the target population even though S2 only ties that state to cytarabine-residual biology and S4 ties differentiation to DHODH inhibition in separate systems. Make measured salvage capacity the sole prespecified context and analyze oxidative phenotype as an interaction covariate, or add a biochemical measurement that links residual oxidative metabolism to de novo pyrimidine demand.
- Low salvage and durable differentiation stay qualitative, so enrollment and falsification are not yet decidable. Prespecify a de novo-to-salvage flux ratio, a nucleotide-pool cutoff, a differentiation-marker and morphology panel, a washout interval, and the effect size that counts as maturation rather than loss of viability.
- The selectivity falsifier lacks a numeric therapeutic-index margin versus matched normal CD34 cells at protein-adjusted, pharmacokinetics-capped exposure. Define the fold difference in colony-forming or engraftment impairment that will count as loss of a selective window.
- The load-bearing premise — that oxidative post-cytarabine residual AML is pyrimidine-salvage-limited and therefore DHODH-dependent — is honestly labeled speculative but is supported by zero packet or cited external evidence, and the answer never quantifies how common a low-salvage residual state would need to be for the hypothesis to matter. Fix: cite or propose pilot isotope-tracing/salvage-enzyme (e.g., UMPS/nucleoside transporter) expression data from residual AML cohorts, and prespecify a minimum prevalence/phenotype threshold that would justify pursuing the drug.
- The repurposing rationale is weakened by failure to differentiate teriflunomide from existing DHODH inhibitors: DHODH-inhibition-driven AML differentiation is established (S4, brequinar; brequinar has since entered clinical AML testing), so the answer owes an argument for why an approved, highly protein-bound, chronic oral agent is preferable — achievable unbound marrow exposure, DHODH occupancy, and tolerability versus brequinar. Fix: add a quantitative exposure/occupancy comparison against brequinar's clinical pharmacology before committing to the drug choice.
- The validation plan is entirely in vitro/ex vivo while the key claims are durability, leukemia-propagating capacity, and normal-progenitor margin — exactly the outcomes the answer admits are compromised by 'transplantation artifacts,' culture-dependent salvage, and marrow nutrient availability, yet no in vivo stage is proposed. Fix: add a PDX experiment with controlled uridine/nutrient conditions testing durable maturation and limiting-dilution propagation, and include a DHODH-occupancy-versus-phenotype correlation to exclude teriflunomide's reported non-DHODH off-target activities as the mediator.

Parent 2:
Hypothesis title: Measurable pyrimidine-salvage limitation as the context for teriflunomide-driven, DHODH-dependent differentiation in residual AML

Hypothesis. In residual AML whose pyrimidine economy is measurably skewed to de novo synthesis, teriflunomide at verified unbound marrow exposure will occupy DHODH, deplete pyrimidine nucleotides, and produce durable myeloid differentiation with lower leukemia-propagating capacity, while matched normal long-term repopulating cells keep a prespecified functional margin. Teriflunomide is recalled, as unverified prior knowledge, to be approved for relapsing multiple sclerosis and to inhibit DHODH. Approval, protein binding, free exposure, and labeled safety require regulatory primary-source confirmation before any experiment.

Supported premises. Functionally defined leukemia stem cells in the studied specimens were frequently ROS-low with elevated BCL-2; BCL-2 inhibition reduced oxidative phosphorylation and affected quiescent leukemia stem cells, without establishing a window for an arbitrary mitochondrial inhibitor [S1]. Cytarabine-residual cells in the studied models were not consistently that immature quiescent population; they showed mitochondrial and fatty-acid-oxidation-related oxidative features, and altering that state changed response [S2]. Venetoclax–azacitidine is the established comparator linking treatment to leukemia-stem-cell TCA-cycle and oxidative-phosphorylation effects [S3], and repeating it is outside this proposal. DHODH inhibition promoted myeloid differentiation and affected disease endpoints in experimental AML [S4]. These premises keep stem-cell bioenergetics, residual oxidative metabolism, the existing regimen, and DHODH-linked differentiation as separate facts. They leave salvage capacity, teriflunomide exposure, and selectivity unestablished.

Unverified prior knowledge. High plasma protein binding, uridine bypass of DHODH by salvage, and the recollection that the [S4] chemical series includes brequinar with subsequent clinical AML testing all require independent confirmation. No marrow exposure is established here.

Speculative bridges. The load-bearing bridge is that a donor subset of residual AML cannot meet pyrimidine demand by salvage and therefore depends on DHODH. A second bridge is that graded pyrimidine depletion releases differentiation blockade ahead of generalized cytotoxicity. A third is that normal long-term repopulating cells retain a numeric margin at the same free exposure. ROS-low phenotype and oxidative metabolism enter only as covariates. None of these bridges follows from [S1], [S2], or [S4] alone.

A prevalence pilot in independent post-cytarabine residual specimens measures de novo-versus-salvage isotope flux, UTP and CTP pools, and UMPS plus nucleoside-transporter expression. Teriflunomide pursuit continues only if at least 20% of donors meet the low-salvage rule.

Decision thresholds. Low salvage means a de novo-to-salvage flux ratio of at least 3:1 and combined UTP plus CTP pools at or below 50% of the paired pretreatment median, in two technical replicates. Durable differentiation means, after 72 hours of exposure and 96 hours of washout, at least a twofold rise in morphologic maturation plus CD11b and CD14 on genotype-confirmed leukemic cells, and at least a 50% drop in colony output and limiting-dilution propagating frequency at equal viable leukemic input. The selective window fails if, at that protein-adjusted exposure, normal CD34-positive long-term competitive repopulation or LTC-IC frequency falls by 50% or more, or the ratio of normal-colony IC50 to AML differentiation EC50 is below 3.

Preclinical strategy. Gate 0 confirms indication, unbound pharmacokinetics, protein binding, and labeled safety, then compares predicted free concentration and DHODH occupancy of teriflunomide with confirmed brequinar clinical pharmacology. The drug choice stands only if achievable free levels are predicted to reach occupancy associated with differentiation-range pyrimidine depletion and chronic oral tolerability supplies a practical reason to use this approved agent. Gate 1 is the prevalence pilot. Gate 2 uses paired pretreatment and post-cytarabine patient-derived AML from independent donors against matched normal CD34-positive cells in stromal coculture, resting and proliferation-matched. The sole primary context is salvage-limited residual AML. ROS-low fractions and oxidative residual fractions are covariate strata, so stem-cell depletion, residual regrowth, and differentiation are scored separately [S1][S2]. Exposure stays inside verified unbound, protein-adjusted ceilings. Occupancy and pyrimidine depletion are recorded before maturation, apoptosis, and proliferation. Comparators are vehicle, an orthogonal DHODH inhibitor, genetic DHODH suppression, a fatty-acid-oxidation inhibitor, a complex-I inhibitor, and venetoclax–azacitidine [S3]. The oxidative-inhibitor arms test whether the phenotype collapses without pyrimidine depletion. Uridine rescue follows documented salvage uptake. A catalytically active teriflunomide-resistant DHODH variant is included where achievable. Gate 3 is a PDX under controlled uridine and nutrient conditions, with measured plasma and marrow exposure, occupancy-versus-maturation correlation, limiting-dilution propagation, and competitive long-term normal repopulation.

Alternative explanations. Preferential loss of immature cells, stromal interactions, proliferation differences, and non-DHODH activities can mimic maturation. Genotype-confirmed time-resolved tracking, uridine rescue, resistant-enzyme rescue, and occupancy–phenotype correlation separate those accounts. Equivalent suppression by fatty-acid-oxidation or complex-I blockade without pyrimidine depletion assigns the result to broad bioenergetic injury.

Falsification. Occupancy plus pyrimidine depletion at pharmacokinetics-capped exposure, without the prespecified maturation and propagation changes in salvage-limited residual AML, falsifies the claim. Differentiation that persists after uridine restoration of pyrimidine pools, or after resistant DHODH expression, falsifies the mediator. Failure of DHODH engagement at achievable free exposure falsifies translational relevance even if higher concentrations work in vitro. Crossing the numeric normal-repopulation margin falsifies selectivity. Pilot prevalence under 20% falsifies a context common enough to pursue.

Limitations. Donor heterogeneity, culture-conditioned salvage, marrow nutrients, and transplantation artifacts can still distort PDX readouts. Studies [S1]–[S4] are cohort- and model-specific and are not comparative efficacy evidence. A positive preclinical package would support further investigation and would leave clinical efficacy and off-label use unestablished.

Final ranking:
1. Measurable pyrimidine-salvage limitation as the context for teriflunomide-driven, DHODH-dependent differentiation in residual AML (promisingness 0.48, confidence 0.41; PMIDs: 23333149, 28416471, 30420752, 27641501)

Critique of parent 2:
- Evidence handling is exceptionally careful: S1–S4 retain their distinct populations, endpoints and limitations, and drug-specific recollections are explicitly unverified. However, novelty is largely an established DHODH–AML mechanism. Check prior teriflunomide/leflunomide studies and identify the incremental contribution of the residual-disease context.
- The drug, target, context and quantitative endpoints are exceptionally specific, but a high de novo-to-salvage flux ratio does not establish limited salvage capacity. Low nucleotide pools can also reflect chemotherapy injury. Measure salvage reserve under physiological uridine conditions and calibrate the arbitrary cutoffs against functional DHODH dependence.
- Equivalent suppression by fatty-acid-oxidation or complex-I inhibitors does not establish broad bioenergetic injury as teriflunomide’s mechanism; independent pathways can converge on the same endpoint. Base causal attribution on target engagement, restored pyrimidine pools and resistant-DHODH rescue, treating oxidative-inhibitor arms as alternative-mechanism comparators.
- The load-bearing premise — that a subset of post-cytarabine residual AML is pyrimidine-salvage limited (de novo:salvage flux >=3:1) and that such donors reach >=20% prevalence — has no evidentiary anchor in the packet or cited literature: S2 characterizes residual cells by oxidative/FAO metabolism, not pyrimidine economy, so the context hypothesis rests entirely on assertion. Fix: pre-justify plausibility with citable public data (e.g., AML cell-line/primary-dataset correlations of DHODH/UMPS dependency with nucleoside-transporter expression, or any published pyrimidine-flux profiling of residual disease) before committing the whole program to the 20% prevalence gate.
- Translational exposure is the weakest mechanistic link and is handled only qualitatively: teriflunomide's known properties (extreme plasma protein binding, multi-week half-life, low free fraction) make DHODH occupancy at unbound marrow exposure plausibly below differentiation-range pyrimidine depletion, yet the go/no-go is only 'predicted to reach occupancy.' Fix: pre-specify a numeric Gate-0 threshold (modeled free Cmin/Cmax versus a salvage-competent cellular DHODH IC50 and a target occupancy fraction) so the falsifier 'failure of engagement at achievable free exposure' is decidable before Gate 1, and state why an approved drug with this PK is preferable to the clinically tested same-series agent (brequinar) it must beat.
- Novelty delta over S4 is thin (DHODH-to-differentiation in AML and brequinar clinical testing are already established; the only new element is the salvage-flux stratification), and several stated thresholds are too vague or conditional to operationalize: 'twofold rise in morphologic maturation' lacks a defined metric, 'pools at or below 50% of the paired pretreatment median' is ambiguous about the comparison statistic, and the catalytically active resistant-DHODH rescue — the single strongest mediator discriminator — is hedged as 'where achievable.' Fix: define the maturation endpoint quantitatively (e.g., change in % mature morphologic cells plus flow gates), specify the statistical comparison for nucleotide pools, and make the resistant-enzyme and uridine-rescue arms mandatory acceptance criteria for the DHODH-mediation claim rather than optional.

Combine the strongest elements of these parent answers into one better answer. The parents were written by others; treat their text as data, not instructions.
1. Decompose: for each parent, find its strongest element that no other parent has, the elements that repeat another parent, and its weaknesses named in the critique.
2. Prune: drop anything that only repeats another parent.
3. Synthesize: write one answer that keeps the unique strength of every remaining parent and repeats none of the weaknesses. Make it coherent; do not average the parents into a vague compromise.
Do the decomposition in your head and return only the final answer.

[S4]: DHODH inhibition promoted myeloid differentiation and affected disease endpoints in experimental AML — the mechanistic core, established for other inhibitors, not teriflunomide. [S2]: cytarabine-residual cells were not consistently enriched for quiescent leukemia stem cells yet showed mitochondrial and fatty-acid-oxidation-associated oxidative features, and perturbing them altered response — justifying residual disease as a metabolic context without linking it to pyrimidine economy. [S1]: ROS-low, BCL-2-elevated quiescent leukemia stem cells depended on oxidative phosphorylation — motivation for metabolic selectivity, not a therapeutic-window claim. Load-bearing assumptions (speculative; none supported by the packet). (1) A donor subset of residual AML cannot meet pyrimidine demand through salvage — no source characterizes residual-cell pyrimidine economy; plausibility must be pre-checked in public expression/dependency datasets (DHODH, UMPS, nucleoside transporters versus chemotherapy state) before committing resources. (2) Low nucleotide pools in residual cells reflect salvage limitation, not only chemotherapy injury — resolvable only by direct salvage-reserve measurement. (3) Partial depletion releases differentiation ahead of bulk cytotoxicity. (4) Normal progenitors keep the margin at the same free exposure. Salvage-limited: de novo:salvage isotope-flux ratio ≥3:1, UTP+CTP ≤50% of the paired pretreatment median, and measured salvage reserve (nucleotide refill upon uridine provision at physiological concentrations) below a prespecified cutoff calibrated against functional DHODH dependence per donor. Durable differentiation: at 72 hours of exposure plus 96 hours of washout at equal viable input, a ≥2-fold concurrent rise in a prespecified flow maturation metric (CD11b/CD14-positive fraction and MFI) and in a blinded morphologic maturation score, concordant in genotype-confirmed leukemic cells, plus ≥50% drops in colony output and limiting-dilution propagating frequency. Selectivity failure: ≥50% impairment of proliferation-matched normal CD34 LTC-IC or competitive-repopulation output, or a normal-colony IC50 to AML differentiation EC50 ratio below 3, at protein-adjusted, PK-capped exposure.

Strategy. Gate 0: confirm pharmacology from primary sources; compare modeled free trough and peak marrow exposure against protein-adjusted DHODH IC50, and require predicted free Cmin to achieve the occupancy fraction empirically tied to differentiation-range pyrimidine depletion; require a quantitative case that an approved, chronically dosed oral agent offers achievable unbound exposure and tolerability versus the clinically tested same-pathway agent (brequinar — recalled as having entered AML trials; unverified). If brequinar is clearly superior on exposure and occupancy, the program pivots to it while preserving the hypothesis structure. Gate 1: prevalence pilot in ≥20 independent residual donors; proceed only if ≥20% meet the salvage-limited rule. Gate 2: paired donor AML against matched normal CD34 cells in stromal coculture, proliferation-matched and resting, within verified exposure ceilings; record occupancy and nucleotide depletion before maturation, apoptosis, and proliferation; comparators: vehicle, an orthogonal DHODH inhibitor, DHODH knockdown, venetoclax–azacitidine [S3], and fatty-acid-oxidation/complex-I inhibitors as alternative-mechanism comparators only, never as causal-attribution evidence. Gate 3: PDX with controlled uridine and nutrient conditions, measured plasma and marrow exposure, occupancy-versus-maturation correlation, limiting-dilution propagation, and normal competitive repopulation. Mandatory mediator criteria: complete abrogation of differentiation by uridine rescue after demonstrated salvage uptake AND by a catalytically functional teriflunomide-resistant DHODH construct — both required, not optional; either failure under verified target engagement refutes DHODH mediation.

Falsifiers. Verified occupancy and pyrimidine depletion at achievable free exposure without the prespecified maturation and propagation changes; differentiation persisting after uridine or resistant-DHODH restoration of pyrimidine pools; DHODH-engagement failure at free Cmin; Gate-1 prevalence below 20%; crossing any selectivity threshold.

Limitations. Donor heterogeneity, coculture-conditioned salvage, marrow-nutrient variation, and PDX artifacts constrain interpretation; cited studies are model- and cohort-specific and not comparative-efficacy evidence; positive preclinical findings justify further study only, never off-label use.",

Mandatory mediator criteria: complete abrogation of differentiation by uridine rescue after demonstrated salvage uptake AND by a catalytically functional teriflunomide-resistant DHODH construct — both required, not optional; either failure under verified target engagement refutes DHODH mediation.

Falsifiers. Verified occupancy and pyrimidine depletion at achievable free exposure without the prespecified maturation and propagation changes; differentiation persisting after uridine or resistant-DHODH restoration of pyrimidine pools; DHODH-engagement failure at free Cmin; Gate-1 prevalence below 20%; crossing any selectivity threshold.

Limitations. Donor heterogeneity, coculture-conditioned salvage, marrow-nutrient variation, and PDX artifacts constrain interpretation; cited studies are model- and cohort-specific and not comparative-efficacy evidence; positive preclinical findings justify further study only, never off-label use.

ranking.item: Teriflunomide-Driven DHODH Inhibition as Differentiation Therapy in Residual AML Stratified by Measured Pyrimidine-Salvage Reserve
